sense: a part of a place: a region, a neighbourhood

evidence: Cic. Att. 15.16a: haec loca venusta sunt
terms.comment: The plural of locus for a stretch of country: in hīs locīs, in these parts, in this area.

evidence: Liv. 22.46.9: regiōnis incolae, the people of the area
Plin. NH 3.46: discrīptiōnemque ab eō factam Ītaliae tōtīus in regiōnēs XI
terms.comment: The word for a larger region, and for an administrative one: Augustus divided Italy into eleven regiōnēs (Plin. NH 3.46) and Rome into fourteen (Plin. NH 3.66).
Terence’s genitive of place: hīc vīcīniae, here in the neighbourhood.

terms.gloss: an open space: a yard, a building plot, a threshing floor
evidence: Dig. 50.16.211: locus sine aedificiō in urbe ārea (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. square, piazza; s.v. yard
terms.comment: A false friend: never a region. Traupman’s ārea portāria and ārea poenālis, the goal and penalty areas (Traupman 50), keep the classical sense of a marked-out open space.

terms.gloss: a zone of the earth; classically also a girdle
evidence: M-O s.v. time zone: zōna temporālis (after Egger)
terms.comment: Greek ζώνη, a girdle; classically one of the five belts into which the earth was divided, from torrid to frozen (Lewis & Short). For a zone in a town or on a map (a pedestrian zone, a danger zone) regiō or loca says it in classical Latin.

phrases.latin: vāstae tum in hīs locīs sōlitūdinēs erant
phrases.english: in those days this whole area was wilderness

phrases.latin: modo quandam vīdī virginem hīc vīcīniae
phrases.english: just now I saw a girl here in the neighbourhood

phrases.latin: in Lūsitāniā ad ōceanum in eā regiōne, ubi est oppidum Olisīpō, monte Tagrō quaedam ē ventō concipiunt certō tempore equae
phrases.english: in Lusitania by the ocean, in the region where the town of Olisipo lies, on Mount Tagrus, some mares conceive from the wind at a certain season
